title: Choose the visual world for Tip-Off Desk (sport-agnostic)
question: A fresh hand, all of it sport-agnostic: NBA first, other sports later. Keep the lead, take an alternate, or re-roll again.

options.label: Form Guide
options.lineage: the handicapper's form guide: past-performance lines, figure boxes, highlighter and ballpoint
options.thesis: Every market reads like a past-performance line, and the desk is marked up the way a handicapper marks a form guide.
options.viewport: Edge Board as dense form lines grouped by game: each market shows its recent results against the line and its open, bet and close prices on one row; the edge sits in a boxed figure; what clears is highlighted, and your added legs are circled in ballpoint blue; tonight's card docked right.
options.risk: Its source is horse racing; it has to read as handicapping in general, not the track, and dense agate can tip into a newspaper costume.

raised.raise: Edge size is encoded on one fixed ramp everywhere it appears, never rescaled per night.
The nightly risk cap is a hard capacity the card visibly fills, like a tape side that cannot overflow.
On the phone, one stale market owns the screen and the next is one swipe away.
One number per screen is set at full display scale; everything else stays small and dense.

options.label: Games System
options.lineage: Otl Aicher's Munich 1972 Olympic identity: one system for every sport
options.thesis: One identity built to hold every sport: each league gets a pictogram and a color zone on a strict grid.
options.viewport: A light shell with a league switcher of pictograms (NBA live, others greyed as coming later); the Edge Board in the league's color zone; prices in tabular figures; the card docked right on the same grid.
options.risk: Familiar to designers: the Munich system is widely imitated, and a timid pastel rendition reads as a stock template.

options.label: Line Map
options.thesis: A price's journey from open to close drawn as a transit line, with Hard Rock's price as the interchange.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue shell; Edge Board table on porcelain panels; the focused market's price path drawn as a line with open, bet and close stations and Hard Rock as the interchange.
options.case: Line movement as routes is exact and sport-neutral, so clarity holds; bettors do not identify with transit.
options.risk: A dark enamel shell plus route lines can crowd dense tables.

options.label: Graphite Console
options.thesis: Persistent graphite panels split by hairline seams; destructive actions sit apart behind deliberate space.
options.viewport: Tiled panels: board, card and checks persist side by side; Clear stands isolated from Lock.
options.case: Clear for a working tool and fully sport-neutral; little identity, close to every dark odds tool.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance as dot size on a fixed magnitude ramp.
options.case: Poetic, but bettors do not read tables as skies.
options.kept: Edge on one fixed ramp everywhere.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Two sides that must not overflow the tape.
options.case: Nostalgic, off-subject for a pricing desk.
options.kept: The risk cap as a visible capacity.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One item owns the screen; the next is one snap away.
options.case: Wrong for a dense desktop board; encourages impulsive swiping.
options.kept: Phone news view: one stale market per screen.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.case: A showcase form, not a working board.
options.kept: One number per screen at display scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What odds tools ship, executed impeccably: a dark dashboard of tables with green and red numbers.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, filter row, dense odds table, card panel on the right.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other odds tool by design.
